design: Existing plain white Arial single-column article; restrained width; no framework, animation, dashboard or reviewer-control UI.
abstract_normalization: Explicit finite TeX typography/math normalization checked against the full original paragraph, not a shortened Zenodo description.

receipt.schema: Original complete receipt; every file retains filename/path/url_from_actual_file_object/final_url/status/headers/file_object/bytes/md5/sha256/utc, and all other original fields. All three actual file entries retained; no name/url/http_status aliases written to the receipt.

future_read_only_view: Authenticate actual metadata.normalized.json against zenodo-record.raw.json and their exact hashes. An in-memory consumer view may expose raw id/metadata/created/updated/files and preserve the complete original normalized object separately. Read the original receipt files by filename; URL is url_from_actual_file_object, HTTP status is status, and complete API metadata is file_object. Use a temporary read-only view only; never create sources/record.json or any aliases, reserialize originals, drop SHA256SUMS or invent transport facts.
checksum_consumer: Authenticate all three published files and the two SHA256SUMS payload entries. The 170-byte checksum file stays at its original source location; its ordinary original Zenodo link needs no extra local page asset. If a future checker uses a narrow authenticated resolver for this text file, it must preserve its complete original file object and must not imply it is a third reader.

metadata_requirements.description: The Fradelizi–Paouris–Schütt second-moment equality characterization extends to every compact full-dimensional convex body, using retained extreme-point simplices.
metadata_requirements.citation_title: Equality in the Fradelizi–Paouris–Schütt second-moment inequality
metadata_requirements.abstract: Fradelizi, Paouris, and Schütt proved a sharp lower bound for the second moment of a convex body whose extreme points lie outside an open Euclidean ball. They characterized equality for polytopes and conjectured the same characterization for arbitrary convex bodies. We prove this conjecture: equality holds precisely for nondegenerate simplices whose vertices lie on the bounding sphere. The proof extends their simplex argument by an almost-everywhere partition into countably many simplices with extreme-point vertices. An exact nonnegative deficit identity retains the equality information for this partition.

complete_original_verdicts: promotion.json reviews.*.verdict stores the full original object; root_authority_entry and root_clearance_record are separate exact authorities. Original pending/null/false history is not converted into a PASS.
public_exclusions: No internal audit counts, hashes, acquisition failures, root review dates, custody history, review controls or reviewer narratives. Mathematical theorem dependencies and prior-credit limits remain explicit.
